item.title: Trump officials declare success after Iowa blast
item.description: Preliminary tests from the explosion of 5 tons of a bomb-making chemical show no spread of lead, a dangerous metal tied to brain damage.

media:content.media:title: Debris flies into the air after the Army detonated several tons of highly volatile, degraded lead azide on the grounds of the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Nov. 25, 2026, in Middletown, Iowa. The detonation was delayed several times due to concerns of environmental and health impacts.

item.title: Iowa’s lead bomb is touching a nerve with MAHA
item.description: Environmental health worries were already top of mind in the state with the country's second highest cancer rates. Then came the Army's toxic blast.

media:content.media:title: Rows of fields and farm homes line the perimeter of the Army Iowa Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026.

item.description: The chaotic conclusion of the COP31 conference is turning nations against the process.

item.title: Court clears Army to detonate toxic explosives in Iowa
item.description: Judges rejected environmentalists' challenge to the Army's EPA-authorized emergency permit, acknowledging the public health risks of exploding the degrading bomb-making chemicals.

media:content.media:title: A sign identifying the facility sits inside a fence surrounding the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Nov. 19, 2026, in Middletown, Iowa.

item.dc:creator: By Ellie Borst

item.title: Trump orders hold on Army’s explosive plans in Iowa
item.description: The president ordered the Army not to blow up tons of toxic bomb-making chemicals until a federal appellate court rules on the matter and Democratic Gov.-elect Rob Sand agrees.

media:content.media:title: An aerial view shows homes on November 20, 2026 in Middletown, Iowa. The town, which sits on the edge of the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, faced evacuations because the Army was planning to detonate several tons of highly-volatile lead azide at the facility.
